protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map hard-mic-01. 24 of 24 wells hold what the plate map
  says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3). Reading of the request: rows A and
    B; excess removed from column 10.

Labware for the technique (Serial dilution): nothing to flag.

Where every liquid ended up (ul):
  liquid                             declared delivered in source elsewhere    lost
  broth                                2000.0    1200.1     799.9       0.0     0.0
  antibiotic 1                         1000.0      50.0     950.0       0.0     0.0
  antibiotic 2                         1000.0      50.0     950.0       0.0     0.0
  culture                              2000.0    1100.0     900.0       0.0     0.0

Prep sheet: what to put on the deck before the run.
  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  2    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A1    antibiotic 1                          50.0    1000.0
  2    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A2    antibiotic 2                          50.0    1000.0
  2    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A3    culture                             1100.0    2000.0

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 0.0488281 ul, 0.0976562 ul, 0.195312 ul, 0.390625 ul and 5 more are
below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 48:  p300.aspirate(antib_vol, tubes["A1"])
   At line 48 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 0.0488281 ul, 0.0976562 ul, 0.195312 ul,
   0.390625 ul and 5 more, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 9 times). A pipette
   cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the
   volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: tube
   A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [b0061eb7642b]

   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)

   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)

3. WARNING CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried antibiotic 1 (tube A1 in slot 2) into well A11 in
slot 3 it was never meant for
   line 49:  p300.dispense(antib_vol, plate[well])
   At line 49 the tip touched the liquid in well A11 in slot 3 while it still carried
   antibiotic 1 (tube A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid
   leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that
   liquid into this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold
   different samples, each now holds a little of another.
   Affected: well A11 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 49. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [f7efdc2cfbe4]

6. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: antibiotic 1 (tube A1 in slot 2)
   line 48:  p300.aspirate(antib_vol, tubes["A1"])
   At line 48 the tip went into antibiotic 1 (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried
   broth (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves
   a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that
   were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in
   the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 48 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing

8. NOTE WELL-CAPACITY: Declared more than the well holds: 2000 ul in a 1898 ul well, 1 well
   line 88:  p300.aspirate(50 * n_wells, tubes["A3"])
   At line 88 the robot draws from tube A3 in slot 2, which the protocol declares (line 22)
   to hold 2000 ul; the well holds 1897.79 ul. The prep sheet cannot be followed as written.
   Wells: tube A3 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A3 in slot 2.
   Fix: Declare what the well can really hold, or use a bigger container.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [dd8a1b09b905]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A used tip carried antibiotic 1 (tube A1 in slot 2) into well A11 in slot 3 it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 49 the tip touched the liquid in well A11 in slot 3 while it still carried antibiotic 1 (tube A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 49. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.
